subject: Careers
title: What employers value
objective_verbatim: I can identify at least four behaviours employers value, such as reliability, communication, effort and safety.
outcomes_verbatim: I can identify at least four behaviours employers value, such as reliability, communication, effort and safety.
calendar_note: Year A. Spring 2 Week 1, 2027-02-22 to 2027-02-26. Tuesday 23 February 2027, Tuesday P3. One 40-minute lesson. Spring 2 runs 22 February to Thursday 25 March 2027. Week 5 is four days with no Friday; the Tuesday lesson is unaffected.

outcomes_verbatim: I can identify at least four behaviours employers value, such as reliability, communication, effort and safety.
sources.note: The current brief supplies the exact focuses, outcomes and row mapping. Other scheme columns are not asserted verbatim. Activities and 40-minute sequencing are newly authored in the accepted Spring 1 format.
Read for file shape, timing, tiers, feedback, private response and typed/scribed access conventions.
Read for the six-outcome closing Evidence Sheet grid pattern. Current six outcomes are rows 22–27 and current Week 5 combines rows 26–27.

source_adaptation: Exact owner-supplied focus and outcomes retained. Rows 26 and 27 share the closing Week 5 lesson. Newly authored invented workplace practice, not a quotation of absent sequence/evidence columns.
timing: Use a calm visual start. Read the pupil goal aloud. Explain that all workers and workplaces are made up. Recall a job and choose between leaving a box in a doorway or putting it in its safe place. Take a reason; accept pointing or a scribed reply.

Read the worked example. Think aloud while matching one action to reliability. State all four behaviours and show one short example of each. Check understanding: 'If I do not know the next step, what can I say?'

Read the four scenario cards one at a time. Match them to the four behaviour word cards as a group. Accept more than one match when the pupil explains it. Ensure every pupil identifies all four behaviours, with the chosen support recorded. Use the hinge question. Ask all pupils to show their choice at once. If any pupil chooses the unsafe option, model stopping and asking, then use the parallel hinge. If all choose correctly, ask why the other option is unsafe and fade the word prompt.
Offer the three routes. Read aloud on request. Record the behaviour names a pupil recognises and how they show understanding. Do not judge spelling or handwriting. Give one brief next step.

Invite a pupil to share one action. Ask peers to identify its behaviour. Prompt any missing behaviour so the four are revisited. Return to the success criteria. Use the exit prompt and record a concise note on the Evidence Sheet. Offer an oral answer, pointing or scribing. Link the same skill to any future work task.
timing_basis: Accepted Spring 1 Careers format: 5 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 40. Processing time and short pauses sit inside the total. Slides marked same task time share the 12-minute independent block.

routes.Supported: In your book: match all four word cards to the four action cards. Point or tell an adult. Add one action for each word; an adult may scribe your words.
routes.Independent: In your book: write the four work words. Give one short action for each. Use the word bank if you need it.
routes.Aspire: In your book: name all four work skills and give an action for each. Then choose a new job task. Show how two skills can help at the same time.

cases.title: The agreed task
cases.situation: A worker agrees to put the clean cups away. The worker does the task and tells the team it is done.
cases.question: Which work skill does this show?
cases.reason: The worker does what was agreed and lets the team know.

cases.title: The unclear task
cases.situation: A worker in a made-up packing room is not sure which box to use. The worker asks, 'Which box shall I use?'
cases.question: Which work skill does this show?
cases.reason: The worker asks a clear question instead of guessing.

cases.title: The hard first try
cases.situation: A worker gets a fold wrong. The worker asks for a model, then tries the next fold.
cases.question: Which work skill does this show?
cases.reason: The worker uses help and tries again.

cases.title: The wet floor
cases.situation: A worker sees water on the floor. The worker keeps clear and tells the agreed adult at once.
cases.question: Which work skill does this show?
cases.reason: The worker avoids the hazard and reports it. The worker does not try a task they have not been taught.

worked_example_and_fade.situation: A worker in a made-up shop agrees to sort ten paper bags. The worker sorts the bags, then says, 'The bags are ready.'
worked_example_and_fade.model: I look for what the worker agreed to do. The worker did that task. This shows reliability. The clear message also shows communication.
worked_example_and_fade.faded_example: A worker is not sure how to stack the empty trays. The worker asks, 'Please show me the safe way.' This shows ____ because ____.
worked_example_and_fade.answer: Communication and safety are both valid: the worker asks for the safe method instead of guessing.

adaptations.Cognition and Learning: Pre-teach the four words with one action each. Read one card at a time. Keep the four-word bank visible. Model one match, then fade the model.
adaptations.Communication and Interaction: Offer pointing, oral rehearsal and a choice of two words before all four. Give wait time. Use the same short sentence stem across the lesson.
adaptations.SEMH: Use third-person made-up workers. Let a pupil pass in whole-group talk and answer privately. Praise a specific safe action. Offer a calm reset and a clear route back.
adaptations.Sensory and Physical: Use large print with space between cards. Offer an uncluttered view, a seated role and a scribe. Do not require handling real tools or hazards.
adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Pair each word with a concrete action. Accept an oral answer or drawing and model the short English phrase afterwards.

ta_focus.I do: Point to the behaviour word as it is modelled. Check the pupil can identify one safe action.
ta_focus.We do: Prompt with the word bank before offering a choice. Note all four behaviours recognised and the prompt used.
ta_focus.Independent: Use the prompt ladder. Scribe only the pupil's own words. Fade help and record one next step.

prompt_ladder: 1 Point to the place or instruction. 2 Ask a short question. 3 Rephrase the instruction. 4 Provide a scaffold or choice. 5 Model the first step only, then return the task.

main_hinge.question: A tool looks broken. You have not been taught to fix it. What is the best next step?
choices: A: Try it quickly so the job is done.
B: Keep clear and tell the agreed adult.
main_hinge.reason: Safety comes first. Stop and report a possible hazard.
main_hinge.decision_rule: If any pupil chooses A or cannot explain B, model stop, keep clear and tell. Use the parallel hinge before releasing the task.

parallel_hinge.question: A worker sees a loose cable across a walkway. What should the worker do?
choices: A: Keep clear and tell the agreed adult.
B: Step over it and say nothing.
parallel_hinge.reason: Report the hazard so it can be dealt with safely.

success: I can name four work skills.
I can match each skill to an action.
I can choose a safe next step.

evidence.description: Actual book/typed/pointed/oral response with date, work reference, access, supplied answers, first response, one NS and reply.

assessment: Record actual evidence against each outcome. Shown means evidence covers it with access logged. Partly means some parts shown. Not yet seen includes missing work or a pass; specify which. Do not count an adult model as independent work. Classroom practice is not proof of workplace competence.
private_help_route: Ask a trusted adult for a private talk. Point to HELP, write or use your aid. You may pass, pause and return with help. No personal story is needed.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Book, pointing, an aid, typing or an exact scribe are valid. Read back a scribed reply and allow a change. Record access apart from supplied answers. Plan in any language.

typed_route.heading: Type instead
typed_route.save: Use the usual save routine with lesson code and work reference; share privately.

feedback: VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step; // self-edit; ? read back; E actual evidence saved; R responded. R follows Voice and Audience, one NS and the pupil reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Add to Careers Portfolio. Offer to the Communication portfolio.
where_this_leads: These skills help in a shop, a kitchen, a store room or any future job.
colour_blind_safe: Words and card IDs carry meaning. No colour-only codes.
accreditation: Evidence may contribute to the unit award. Staff confirm actual evidence and mapping; completion is not automatic.
worked_examples_status: All workers, workplace situations and replies are invented. No employer, brand, place or private individual is named.
publication: Only Public replacements and Shared_Resources are intended for public use. Delivery publishes nothing.

Tuesday 23 February 2027 · P3 · 40 minutes · Year A
BUILD Careers · Spring 2 Week 1 · Public edition
What employers value
Unit: Resilience & Change — Work-ready resilience
Theme: Resilience & Change. Five teaching weeks. Week 5 is the closing lesson and brings rows 26 and 27 together. Group: up to five learners. Supported is the default.
Exact lesson outcomes
I can identify at least four behaviours employers value, such as reliability, communication, effort and safety.
Source: BUILD Careers scheme, Spring 2 rows 22. Focus and outcomes supplied verbatim in the current brief.
Prepare and purpose

Teach useful habits with invented, unnamed workplaces. Books, pens, Support Cards, Vocabulary Mat and Evidence Sheet. Print cards as reusable references. No write-on pupil sheets, internet, login or personal phone is needed. Read the exact outcome aloud and explain the short goal.
Where this leads: These skills help in a shop, a kitchen, a store room or any future job.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So; British Values IL/MR. Respectful speech, a private choice of response and safe help-seeking are practised.
Forty minute sequence

table: In your book: write the title or ask for a scribe. Name or draw one job. Point to the safer choice.
Listen. Then say or point: 'Please show me the next step.'
Match each action to a word. Say: 'This shows ... because ...' Choose the safe next step. Tell a partner why.
In your book: name or draw the four ways to do a job well. Add an action for each. Use your route card.
Check: I named four ways. I gave an action. I chose a safe step. Say or point to all four words. Choose one to practise next time.

blocks_in_document_order.paragraph: Teaching and checks
Arrival and retrieval 5 minutes

Use a calm visual start. Read the pupil goal aloud. Explain that all workers and workplaces are made up. Recall a job and choose between leaving a box in a doorway or putting it in its safe place. Take a reason; accept pointing or a scribed reply.
I Do 8 minutes

Read the worked example. Think aloud while matching one action to reliability. State all four behaviours and show one short example of each. Check understanding: 'If I do not know the next step, what can I say?'
We Do 10 minutes

Read the four scenario cards one at a time. Match them to the four behaviour word cards as a group. Accept more than one match when the pupil explains it. Ensure every pupil identifies all four behaviours, with the chosen support recorded. Use the hinge question. Ask all pupils to show their choice at once. If any pupil chooses the unsafe option, model stopping and asking, then use the parallel hinge. If all choose correctly, ask why the other option is unsafe and fade the word prompt.
You Do 12 minutes
Offer the three routes. Read aloud on request. Record the behaviour names a pupil recognises and how they show understanding. Do not judge spelling or handwriting. Give one brief next step.
Review and exit 5 minutes

Invite a pupil to share one action. Ask peers to identify its behaviour. Prompt any missing behaviour so the four are revisited. Return to the success criteria. Use the exit prompt and record a concise note on the Evidence Sheet. Offer an oral answer, pointing or scribing. Link the same skill to any future work task.
Model and fade
I look for what the worker agreed to do. The worker did that task. This shows reliability. The clear message also shows communication.
A worker is not sure how to stack the empty trays. The worker asks, 'Please show me the safe way.' This shows ____ because ____.
Hinge and parallel recheck
Main: A tool looks broken. You have not been taught to fix it. What is the best next step? A: Try it quickly so the job is done.  B: Keep clear and tell the agreed adult. Key B.
Parallel: A worker sees a loose cable across a walkway. What should the worker do? A: Keep clear and tell the agreed adult.  B: Step over it and say nothing. Key A.
If any pupil chooses A or cannot explain B, model stop, keep clear and tell. Use the parallel hinge before releasing the task.
Access evidence and feedback
Supported
In your book: match all four word cards to the four action cards. Point or tell an adult. Add one action for each word; an adult may scribe your words.
Independent

In your book: name all four work skills and give an action for each. Then choose a new job task. Show how two skills can help at the same time.
Planned adaptations

Model and card answers
All workplace cases are invented. Accept equivalent safe language. Do not require a public performance or a personal history.
Card A
Reliability
The worker does what was agreed and lets the team know.
Card B
Communication
The worker asks a clear question instead of guessing.
Card C
Effort
The worker uses help and tries again.
Card D
Safety
The worker avoids the hazard and reports it. The worker does not try a task they have not been taught.
Worked example and fade
I look for what the worker agreed to do. The worker did that task. This shows reliability. The clear message also shows communication.
Communication and safety are both valid: the worker asks for the safe method instead of guessing.
Judgement and safe delivery
Main hinge

A tool looks broken. You have not been taught to fix it. What is the best next step? A: Try it quickly so the job is done.  B: Keep clear and tell the agreed adult. Key B. Safety comes first. Stop and report a possible hazard.
Parallel hinge

A worker sees a loose cable across a walkway. What should the worker do? A: Keep clear and tell the agreed adult.  B: Step over it and say nothing. Key A. Report the hazard so it can be dealt with safely.
If any pupil chooses A or cannot explain B, model stop, keep clear and tell. Use the parallel hinge before releasing the task.
What to retain

Reliability and an action; Communication and an action; Effort and an action; Safety and an action. Record the actual words or selections, first attempt, work reference, usual access, supplied choices and answers, one NS and reply. Spelling and handwriting are not the target.
Common errors
Effort means keep going even when a task is unsafe. Effort includes stopping, asking for help and using the safe steps.
Asking for help means I am bad at the job. A clear question helps a worker do a task well and safely.

blocks_in_document_order.paragraph: Teaching and checks
Arrival and retrieval 5 minutes

Use a calm visual start. Read the pupil goal aloud. Explain that all workers and workplaces are made up. Recall a job and choose between leaving a box in a doorway or putting it in its safe place. Take a reason; accept pointing or a scribed reply.
I Do 8 minutes

Read the worked example. Think aloud while matching one action to reliability. State all four behaviours and show one short example of each. Check understanding: 'If I do not know the next step, what can I say?'
We Do 10 minutes

Read the four scenario cards one at a time. Match them to the four behaviour word cards as a group. Accept more than one match when the pupil explains it. Ensure every pupil identifies all four behaviours, with the chosen support recorded. Use the hinge question. Ask all pupils to show their choice at once. If any pupil chooses the unsafe option, model stopping and asking, then use the parallel hinge. If all choose correctly, ask why the other option is unsafe and fade the word prompt.
You Do 12 minutes
Offer the three routes. Read aloud on request. Record the behaviour names a pupil recognises and how they show understanding. Do not judge spelling or handwriting. Give one brief next step.
Review and exit 5 minutes

Invite a pupil to share one action. Ask peers to identify its behaviour. Prompt any missing behaviour so the four are revisited. Return to the success criteria. Use the exit prompt and record a concise note on the Evidence Sheet. Offer an oral answer, pointing or scribing. Link the same skill to any future work task.
